newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Matches scheduled for Wednesday in the English premier league (kick-off 1945 GMT unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Aston Villa (7) v Sheffield Wednesday (8)

Aston Villa hope to end a poor run of form which includes only one win in five league games, and a disappointing 3-1 F.A. Cup fourth round defeat at Derby on Saturday. Striker Ian Taylor is out with a thigh strain while captain Andy Townsend is doubtful with a shoulder injury.

Sheffield Wednesday's former England striker David Hirst has been substituted in favour of youngsters Andy Booth and Richie Humphreys, while Italian Benito Carbone is still doubtful with a groin injury.
Leeds (11) v Derby (15)

Leeds' Ghanian striker Tony Yeboah is struggling with a hamstring injury, but has at least indicated that he will stay at Elland Road until the end of the season, despite reports that he had fallen out with manager George Graham. Teenage midfielder Lee Bowyer is also doubtful with an ankle strain.

Derby will be without defender Jacob Laursen, who twisted a knee in the warm-up to last weekend's 3-1 win at Aston Villa. Gary Rowett (trapped nerve), Daryl Powell (capsular strain) and Matt Carbon are all doubtful after also picking up injuries in that match.
Leicester (13) v Sunderland (12)

Leicester hope to keep up the form that has seen them through to the League Cup quarter-finals and the F.A. Cup fifth round after defeating Ipswich 1-0 and Norwich 2-1 respectively. They are likely to keep faith in utility player Ian Marshall in attack, following his goal against Norwich, but Swedish defender Pontus Kaamark is out with a broken arm.

Sunderland have teenage striker Michael Bridges sidelined after a groin operation, while coach Peter Reid is close to signing defender Alan Johnston for 500,000 pounds ($806,000) from French club Rennes.
Manchester United (2) v Wimbledon (5) (kick-off 2000 GMT)

Manchester United could head the premier league if they beat Wimbledon, who they face for the second time in five days following their 1-1 F.A. Cup draw at Old Trafford on Saturday. United are still without England pair David Beckham (ankle) and Gary Pallister (hamstring), while it has been confirmed Eric Cantona starts a two-match ban on February 15.

Fearless Wimbledon will hope to keep the pressure up on their opponents before their F.A. Cup replay next Tuesday. They are at full strength, but coach Joe Kinnear must decide between Efan Ekoku or Dean Holdsworth to play alongside Marcus Gayle in attack.
Newcastle United (4) v Everton (9)

Newcastle have only the league and the UEFA Cup to concentrate on after their surprise 2-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest in their home F.A. Cup tie on Sunday. England defender Steve Howey has ruled himself out for the rest of the season with a calf injury, while fellow defenders Philippe Albert and John Beresford are also doubtful through injury.

Everton, who have won only once in five premier league games, could be off-loading Andrei Kanchelskis to Italian club Fiorentina in a reported eight million pounds deal. The Ukranian winger has struggled to form an effective partnership with Scottish striker Duncan Ferguson, and is doubtful with a bruised foot.
Nottingham Forest (17) v Coventry (16)

Forest boast the best recent record in the premier league with five straight victories and new coach Stuart Pearce is in line for the prestigious "manager of the month" award. Welsh striker Dean Saunders is still doubtful with a hamstring injury picked up against Chelsea, while Nigel Clough looks set to return after being cup-tied in the 2-1 win against Newcastle.
Coventry hope to parade Ukranian defender Aleksandr Evtushok following his signing from Dnepr for approximately 800,000 pounds on Monday after the club sold Reggie Genaux to Udinese.
Tottenham (10) v Blackburn (14)
Tottenham's England attackers Teddy Sheringham and Darren Anderton received contrasting news on their injury problems.

Sheringham aggravated his ankle injury in training on Monday and looks certain to be out of club action and England's World Cup qualifying match against Italy on February 12. Winger Anderton is getting back to match fitness, after playing for Spurs' reserves twice in four days, following knee ligament damage.

Blackburn have had an attempt to capture Polish international striker Marek Citko on-loan from Widzew Lodz until the end of the season rejected, with the Polish champions saying they only wanted a cash deal.
West Ham (18) v Arsenal (3)

Troubled West Ham were embarrassed by second division strugglers Wrexham in their 1-0 F.A. Cup defeat at home on Saturday. After coach Harry Redknapp's offer to resign was rejected, he is now looking to buy two strikers to solve their goal drought, with Wimbledon's Dean Holdsworth at the top of his list.
London rivals Arsenal welcome back Welsh striker John Hartson after a two match ban, but Dutchman Dennis Bergkamp is suspended. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
